dialect.detail: JMA ORCA medical receipt system (JMA standard receipt software), compiled with GnuCOBOL/OpenCOBOL on Linux. Uses COPY with REPLACING using // delimiters, INDEXED files with DYNAMIC/SEQUENTIAL access, typical of GnuCOBOL-based ORCA system.
evidence: INDEXED file organization with DYNAMIC and SEQUENTIAL ACCESS MODE

purpose.domain_detail: Japanese medical insurance receipt (レセプト) processing system - specifically diagnosis classification point aggregation for hospitalization (入院) claims including long-term care and self-pay patients
purpose.summary: ORCR0840 is a batch program in the JMA ORCA medical receipt software system that aggregates and edits diagnosis classification point scores for inpatient (hospitalization) receipt claims. It processes multiple indexed ISAM files (RECE82, RECE84, RECE85, RECE8A, RECE8B) representing receipt data and writes error records. The program has an extensive revision history spanning 2003-2010 covering Japanese medical fee revisions.

notable_features: 45 COPY statements with REPLACING using // delimiter
Multiple INDEXED files with both DYNAMIC and SEQUENTIAL access modes on same physical file
No EXEC SQL or EXEC CICS
473 PERFORM statements indicating structured procedural decomposition
Extensive Japanese-language comments (EUC-JP encoded, decoded as latin-1)
Long revision history with version numbers (01.00.01 through 04.04.14)
Fixed format with max line length 80
verdict.notes: Comments are in Japanese EUC-JP encoding but the file was decoded as latin-1, causing mojibake in the comment text. The code itself is syntactically intact. This is clearly part of the well-known open-source JMA ORCA medical receipt system developed by NaCl (Japan). File size ~485KB with 10027 lines indicates a large, complex production program.
